issues.t: Oil sludge and loss of oil pressure
issues.sym: The oil pressure gauge drops low or flickers, especially at idle when hot, the oil light comes on, or the engine starts knocking. In bad cases the engine seizes.
issues.why: Thick sludge builds up in the oil pan and blocks the screen on the oil pump pickup, so the pump can no longer draw enough oil. Long oil change intervals and heat make it worse.
issues.next: If the oil light comes on, pull over and shut the engine off. Have a shop drop the oil pan and clean the pickup screen before the bearings are damaged. Afterwards, change the oil and filter often.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle and tensioner failure
issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the engine for a few seconds at start-up, a check engine light with cam/crank timing codes (P0011 to P0017), misfires or a drop in power.
issues.why: The timing chain tensioner and plastic guides on the 4.7L wear out early, especially when oil changes are skipped or the wrong oil is used. If the chain jumps a tooth the engine can be badly damaged.
issues.next: Do not ignore a start-up rattle. Have the timing codes read and the chain inspected. Replacing the chain, guides and tensioner together is the usual fix.

issues.t: Dropped valve seat causing misfire and lost power
issues.sym: A steady misfire on one cylinder, a flashing or steady check engine light, rough running and lower power. Sometimes the engine suddenly starts ticking or knocking.
issues.why: On these engines a valve seat pressed into the cylinder head can loosen and drop out, usually after the engine has run hot. The valve then cannot seal, and loose pieces can damage the piston.
issues.next: If a misfire stays on one cylinder after new plugs and coils, ask for a compression or leak-down test. Stop driving if there is a new knocking sound. Fixing it means a rebuilt or new cylinder head.

issues.t: Overheating and head gasket failure
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, coolant keeps going down with no visible leak, white sweet-smelling exhaust smoke, or milky oil.
issues.why: The 4.7L is sensitive to heat. A tired water pump, thermostat, fan clutch or radiator lets it run hot, and overheating then damages the head gaskets and valve seats.
issues.next: Stop driving as soon as the gauge rises. Have the cooling system pressure tested and a combustion-gas test done. Fixing the cooling part early is far cheaper than a head gasket job.

issues.t: Intake plenum gasket leak burns oil
issues.sym: The engine uses oil with no outside leak, pings under acceleration, idles rough or misfires, and oil can be seen inside the throttle body. Spark plugs and oxygen sensors foul.
issues.why: The gasket under the stamped-steel plate on the bottom of the Magnum intake manifold fails, so oil vapor from the crankcase is pulled into the engine and burned. Chrysler issued a service bulletin (09-05-00) for it.
issues.next: Have a shop check for oil in the intake and test for the leak. Fix it with an upgraded plate-and-gasket kit rather than just a new paper gasket, so it does not come back.

issues.t: Camshaft position sensor failure
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes like P0340 or P1391, hard starting or no start, rough idle, misfires or stalling.
issues.why: The camshaft position sensor in the distributor gets dirty or fails with age, and the engine computer loses track of timing.
issues.next: Have the codes read. The sensor is inexpensive and quick to replace; do not keep driving if the engine stalls in traffic.

issues.t: Broken exhaust manifold bolts cause ticking
issues.sym: A ticking or puffing noise from the engine bay that is loudest on a cold start and may fade as the engine warms up. Sometimes an exhaust smell.
issues.why: The bolts holding the exhaust manifolds to the cylinder heads rust and snap from repeated heating and cooling, letting exhaust leak at the joint.
issues.next: Not urgent, but have it fixed before more bolts break or the gasket burns through. Keep exhaust fumes out of the cab.

issues.t: Stalling while driving from crank sensor fault
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or coasting to a stop, idles rough, or cranks but will not start until it sits for a while.
issues.why: On these trucks the crankshaft position sensor or its wiring connection fails, so the engine computer loses the signal it needs to run the engine. Owners also report a loose engine computer connector causing the same thing.
issues.next: Have codes read right after a stall. A shop can check the crank sensor signal and its connector; replacing the sensor is a common first fix.

issues.t: Radiator leaks and overheating
issues.sym: Coolant on the ground at the front of the truck, low coolant, the temperature gauge rising, or steam from the radiator.
issues.why: The radiators on these trucks crack and leak with age. The transmission cooler lines at the radiator can also start to leak.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the temperature gauge and do not drive if it runs hot. Have the radiator and cooler lines pressure tested and replace the radiator if it is leaking.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Slipping when accelerating hard or going uphill, late or harsh shifts, the transmission stuck in one gear (limp mode), no reverse, or the truck not moving in gear.
issues.why: The automatics in the Dakota wear out from heat, especially when towing or hauling, and the torque converter can fail. Old fluid speeds up the wear.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell right away. If it slips or goes into limp mode, have codes read and get a transmission diagnosis before driving much more.

issues.t: Transfer case output seal leak (4x4)
issues.sym: Red fluid dripping from the middle of the truck, a burning smell, grinding when shifting into 4WD, or a whine at highway speed.
issues.why: The rubber seals where the driveshafts leave the transfer case dry out and crack with heat and age.
issues.next: Check the transfer case fluid level and have the leaking seal replaced before the case runs low and gets damaged.

issues.t: Upper ball joint wear and separation (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front end over bumps or when turning, loose steering, and in the worst case a front wheel that collapses inward.
issues.why: Water gets into the front upper ball joints of 4x4 trucks, rusts them and wears them out early. A badly worn joint can pull apart. Recall 04V-596 covers 2000–2003 4x4 Dakotas.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the front end clunks or the steering feels loose, have the ball joints inspected right away.

issues.t: Front ball joints wear out early
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end, loose or wandering steering, uneven tire wear, or a wobble at speed.
issues.why: The factory upper and lower ball joints are sealed and wear out quickly once their boots tear and water gets in, often well before 100,000 miles. A separated joint can let a wheel fold under.
issues.next: Have the front end checked if you hear clunks. Replace worn joints in pairs and get an alignment afterwards.

issues.t: Lower ball joints, tie rods and sway bar links wear
issues.sym: Clunking or knocking over bumps, steering that feels loose, a pull to one side, or uneven tire wear. Some owners had a lower ball joint break.
issues.why: The front lower ball joints, outer tie rod ends and sway bar end links on this generation wear out, and owners report replacing them from about 35,000 miles on.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected at the first clunk. A broken ball joint can make you lose control, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing or hub failure
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that grows with speed, a looseness in the front wheel, or an ABS light.
issues.why: The front wheel bearings and hub units on these trucks wear out, sometimes quite early.
issues.next: Have the wheel checked for play. A failing bearing can overheat and seize, so replace it soon.

issues.t: Front brake locks up and wheel overheats
issues.sym: The truck pulls to one side, a front wheel gets very hot or smokes, there is a burning smell, and the pads or rotor on that side burn up.
issues.why: A front caliper sticks and stays clamped, or a collapsed brake hose holds pressure on it. The brake then drags until it cools down.
issues.next: If a wheel smokes or the truck pulls hard, stop and let it cool. Have the calipers and hoses checked; replace the caliper, hose, pads and rotor on that side.

issues.t: Steering wheel shake when braking from warped rotors
issues.sym: The steering wheel or truck shakes when braking from highway speed, sometimes with a pulsing pedal or a dragging, hot front wheel.
issues.why: The front rotors warp from heat, often because a front caliper does not fully release.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected. Replace rotors and pads, and the caliper if it is sticking.

issues.t: Clicking behind dash and wrong air temperature
issues.sym: A repeated clicking or ticking from behind the dashboard, or air that stays hot or cold no matter where the knob is set.
issues.why: A plastic blend door actuator motor inside the heater box strips its gears or fails.
issues.next: Not a safety problem. Have the actuator replaced; on many trucks it can be reached from under the dash.

issues.t: Power window regulator breaks
issues.sym: The window drops into the door, moves slowly or crooked, or the motor runs but the glass does not move.
issues.why: The window regulator uses plastic parts that become brittle, especially in hot weather, and break.
issues.next: Tape or prop the glass up to keep weather out and have the regulator replaced. Metal aftermarket regulators are an option.

issues.t: Paint peeling off
issues.sym: The paint or clear coat flakes and peels, usually on the hood, roof and other surfaces that get the most sun.
issues.why: The factory paint finish loses adhesion and lets go of the primer after years of sun exposure.
issues.next: Cosmetic only. Wash and wax to slow it, and get quotes for repainting the affected panels if it bothers you.

issues.t: Rust on radiator support and body panels
issues.sym: Bubbling paint on the rear fenders or doors, rust around the wheel wells, and rot on the radiator support under the hood, sometimes hidden by trim.
issues.why: Road salt and trapped moisture rust the radiator support area and lower body panels on these trucks.
issues.next: Inspect under the hood and around the fenders each year, especially in snowy states. Treat rust early; a rotted radiator support should be repaired by a body shop.

issues.t: Takata airbag inflators can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The danger is that in a crash the driver or passenger front airbag inflator can burst and throw metal pieces into the cab.
issues.why: Airbag inflators made by Takata use a propellant that breaks down after years of heat and humidity. Recalls 15V-313 (driver) and 16V-352, 18V-021 and 19V-018 (passenger) cover these Dakotas.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls today and get the free replacement as soon as possible.

issues.t: Rear axle pinion nut can loosen and lock the axle (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or noise from the rear axle. In the worst case the rear wheels lock up while driving.
issues.why: The nut that holds the drive pinion in the rear differential can work loose because not enough thread adhesive was used. Recalls 12V-474 and 13V-038 add a retainer.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free fix done. Get any new rear-axle noise checked promptly.

issues.t: Clockspring can disable driver airbag (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, and the horn or steering wheel controls may stop working.
issues.why: Material inside the steering column clockspring can cut the ribbon wire that carries the airbag signal, so the driver airbag would not deploy. Recall 01V-153.
issues.next: If the airbag light is on, have the codes read and check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Brake tube or hose can be rubbed through (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or low brake pedal, the brake warning light, or brake fluid leaking near a front wheel or the rear axle.
issues.why: The left front brake tube can be worn through by a steering hose, and the rear brake hose can be punctured by the rear axle vent hose. Recalls 00V-193 and 00V-198.
issues.next: If the pedal goes soft or fluid is leaking, do not drive the truck. Check the VIN for these recalls.

issues.t: Transmission fluid can leak onto exhaust (recall)
issues.sym: Transmission fluid drips under the truck, or a burning smell or smoke from underneath.
issues.why: Fluid leaking from the automatic transmission can land on the hot exhaust and catch fire. Recall 00V-197.
issues.next: If you see smoke or smell burning fluid, stop and shut the engine off. Check the VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Wiper, lighting and wiring faults (recalls)
issues.sym: The windshield wipers quit, the exterior lights stop working, or the horn and turn signals act up.
issues.why: Three 2003 recalls: a wiper motor that can fail (04V-216), a central timer module that can shut off the lights (02V-322), and a dash wiring harness that can chafe (03V-389).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have them done for free.

issues.t: Truck may roll away in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter goes into Park but the truck can still roll, or it will not hold in Park.
issues.why: A cup plug that holds the parking pawl shaft in the 42RLE automatic may be installed wrong, so the pawl does not hold. Recall 05V-460 adds a bracket.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake until the recall is checked. Check your VIN.

issues.t: Manual-transmission truck may not start or may lurch (recall)
issues.sym: The engine will not crank with the clutch pressed, or the truck moves when started.
issues.why: Return springs in the clutch ignition interlock switch can break on manual-transmission trucks built July 2005 to July 2006. Recall 14V-795.
issues.next: Check the VIN and have the switch replaced for free. Until then, start the truck with the clutch fully pressed and the parking brake set.

issues.t: Computer faults can lock wheels or affect ABS (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden wheel lock-up or loss of control, or ABS warnings.
issues.why: A 2006 recall (06V-038) fixed an ABS control unit fault, and a 2007 recall (06V-341) reprogrammed the engine computer because the drive wheels could briefly lock.
issues.next: Check your VIN to confirm the software updates were done.
